source_text: Ἣν εἶδον, ἀδελφοί, τοιαύτη. νηστεύσας πολλάκις καὶ δεηθεὶς τοῦ κυρίου, ἵνα μοι φανερώσῃ τὴν ἀποκάλυψιν, ἥν μοι ἐπηγγείλατο δεῖξαι διὰ τῆς πρεσβυτέρας ἐκείνης, αὐτῇ τῇ νυκτί μοι ὦπται ἡ πρεσβυτέρα καὶ εἶπέν μοι: Ἐπεὶ οὕτως ἐνδεὴς εἶ καὶ σπουδαῖος εἰς τὸ γνῶναι πάντα, ἐλθὲ εἰς τὸν ἀγρόν, ὅπου χονδρίζεις, καὶ περὶ ὥραν πέμπτην ἐμφανισθήσομαί σοι καὶ δείξω σοι, ἃ δεῖ σε ἰδεῖν. ἠρώτησα αὐτὴν λέγων: Κυρία, εἰς ποῖον τόπον τοῦ ἀγροῦ; Ὅπου, φησίν, θέλεις. ἐξελεξάμην τόπον καλὸν ἀνακεχωρηκότα. πρὶν δὲ λαλῆσαι αὐτῇ καὶ εἰπεῖν τὸν τόπον, λέγει μοι: Ἥξω ἐκεῖ, ὅπου θέλεις. ἐγενόμην οὖν, ἀδελφοί, εἰς τὸν ἀγρὸν καὶ συνεψήφισα τὰς ὥρας καὶ ἦλθον εἰς τὸν τόπον, ὅπου διεταξάμην αὐτῇ ἐλθεῖν, καὶ βλέπω συμψέλιον κείμενον ἐλεφάντινον, καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ συμψελίου ἔκειτο κερβικάριον λινοῦν καὶ ἐπάνω λέντιον ἐξηπλωμένον λινοῦν καρπάσιον. ἰδὼν ταῦτα κείμενα καὶ μηδένα ὄντα ἐν τῷ τόπῳ ἔκθαμβος ἐγενόμην, καὶ ὡσεὶ τρόμος με ἔλαβεν καὶ αἱ τρίχες μου ὀρθαί: καὶ ὡσεὶ φρίκη μοι προσῆλθεν μόνου μου ὄντος. ἐν ἐμαυτῷ οὖν γενόμενος καὶ μνησθεὶς τῆς δόξης τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ λαβὼν θάρσος, θεὶς τὰ γόνατα ἐξωμολογούμην τῷ κυρίῳ πάλιν τὰς ἁμαρτίας μου ὡς καὶ πρότερον. ἡ δὲ ἦλθεν μετὰ νεανίσκων ἕξ, οὓς καὶ πρότερον ἑωράκειν, καὶ ἐστάθη μοι καὶ κατηκροᾶτο προσευχομένου καὶ ἐξομολογουμένου τῷ κυρίῳ τὰς ἁμαρτίας μου. καὶ ἁψαμένη μου λέγει: Ἑρμᾶ, παῦσαι περὶ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν σου πάντα ἐρωτῶν: ἐρώτα καὶ περὶ δικαιοσύνης, ἵνα λάβῃς μέρος τι ἐξ αὐτῆς εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου. καὶ ἐξεγείρει με τῆς χειρὸς καὶ ἄγει με πρὸς τὸ συμψέλιον καὶ λέγει τοῖς νεανίσκοις: Ὑπάγετε καὶ οἰκοδομεῖτε. καὶ μετὰ τὸ ἀναχωρῆσαι τοὺς νεανίσκους καὶ μόνων ἡμῶν γεγονότων λέγει μοι: Κάθισον ὧδε. λέγω αὐτῇ: Κυρία, ἄφες τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους πρῶτον καθίσαι. Ὅ σοι λέγω, φησίν, κάθισον. θέλοντος οὖν μου καθίσαι εἰς τὰ δεξιὰ μέρη οὐκ εἴασέ με, ἀλλ’ ἐννεύει μοι τῇ χειρί, ἵνα εἰς τὰ ἀριστερὰ μέρη καθίσω. διαλογιζομένου μου οὖν καὶ λυπουμένου, ὅτι οὐκ εἴασέ με εἰς τὰ δεξιὰ μέρη καθίσαι, λέγει μοι: Λυπῇ, Ἑρμᾶ; ὁ εἰς τὰ δεξιὰ μέρη τόπος ἄλλων ἐστίν, τῶν ἤδη εὐαρεστηκότων τῷ θεῷ καὶ παθόντων εἵνεκα τοῦ ὀνόματος: σοὶ δὲ πολλὰ λείπει ἵνα μετ’ αὐτῶν καθίσῃς: ἀλλὰ ὡς μένεις τῇ ἁπλότητί σου, μεῖνον, καὶ καθιῇ μετ’ αὐτῶν καὶ ὅσοι ἐὰν ἐργάσωνται τὰ ἐκείνων ἔργα καὶ ὑπενέγκωσιν, ἃ καὶ ἐκεῖνοι ὑπήνεγκαν. Τί, φημί, ὑπήνεγκαν; Ἄκουε, φησίν: μάστιγας, φυλακάς, θλίψεις μεγάλας, σταυρούς, θηρία εἵνεκεν τοῦ ὀνόματος: διὰ τοῦτο ἐκείνων ἐστὶν τὰ δεξιὰ μέρη τοῦ ἁγιάσματος καὶ ὃς ἐὰν πάθῃ διὰ τὸ ὄνομα: τῶν δὲ λοιπῶν τὰ ἀριστερὰ μέρη ἐστίν.
pass_a_gloss: What I saw, brothers, was the following. Having fasted many times and prayed to the Lord, that He might reveal to me the revelation which He had promised to show me through that elderly woman, on that very night the elderly woman appeared to me and said to me: Since you are so needy and eager to know all things, come to the field where you work and around the fifth hour I will appear to you and show you what you must see. I asked her, saying: Lady, to what place in the field? Wherever you wish, she says. I chose a beautiful secluded place. But before I spoke to her and told her the place, she says to me: I will be there, wherever you wish. So I came, brothers, to the field and counted the hours and came to the place where I had told her to come, and I saw a linen cushion lying there and on the cushion a linen cloth was lying and above it a linen carpet was spread out. Seeing these things lying there and no one being in the place, I was amazed and a sort of trembling seized me and my hairs stood on end: and a sort of horror approached me, I being alone. So I came to myself and remembered the glory of God and took courage, and putting my knees on the ground, I confessed to the Lord again my sins, as also before. And she came with six young men, whom I had also seen before, and stood by me and looked at me as I was praying and confessing my sins to the Lord. And touching me, she says: Hermas, stop inquiring about all your sins: inquire also about righteousness, so that you may receive a part of it for your household. And she rouses me with her hand and leads me to the cushion and says to the young men: Go and build. And after the young men departed and we were alone, she says to me: Sit down here. I say to her: Lady, allow the elders to sit down first. Whatever I tell you, she says, sit down. So when I wanted to sit down on the right side, she did not allow me, but signals to me with her hand to sit down on the left side. As I was reasoning and being grieved that she did not allow me to sit down on the right side, she says to me: Are you grieved, Hermas? The place on the right side belongs to others, who have already pleased God and suffered for the sake of the name: you still lack much in order to sit with them: but as you remain in your simplicity, remain, and you will sit with them and whoever works their works and bears what they also bore. What, I say, did they bear? Listen, she says: floggings, imprisonments, great tribulations, crosses, wild beasts for the sake of the name: for this reason the right side of the sanctuary belongs to them, and to whoever suffers for the name: but the left side belongs to the rest.
pass_b_english: What I saw, brothers, was like this. I had fasted many times and prayed to the Lord, asking him to reveal to me the revelation that he had promised to show me through that elderly woman. On that very night the elderly woman appeared to me and said, "Since you are so needy and eager to know all things, come to the field where you work, and around the fifth hour I will appear to you and show you what you must see." I asked her, "Lady, to what place in the field?" She answered, "Wherever you wish." I chose a beautiful, secluded spot. But before I could speak to her and tell her the place, she said to me, "I will be there, wherever you wish." So I went, brothers, to the field, counted the hours, and came to the place where I had arranged for her to come. There I saw a cushion made of elephant ivory lying on the ground, and on the cushion lay a linen cloth, and spread out above it was a linen carpet of fine flax. Seeing these things lying there and no one in the place, I was amazed. A sort of trembling seized me, and my hair stood on end; a sort of horror came over me, because I was alone. I collected myself and remembered the glory of God, took courage, fell to my knees, and confessed my sins to the Lord again, just as I had before. Then she arrived with six young men, whom I had also seen before. They stood by me and watched as I prayed and confessed my sins to the Lord. She touched me and said, "Hermas, stop asking about all your sins. Ask also about righteousness, so that you may receive a share of it for your household." She roused me by the hand and led me to the cushion, and she said to the young men, "Go and build." After the young men left and we were alone, she said to me, "Sit down here." I said to her, "Lady, let the elders sit down first." She replied, "Whatever I tell you, sit down." So when I wanted to sit on the right side, she did not allow me, but signaled with her hand for me to sit on the left side. As I was reasoning and grieving that she would not let me sit on the right, she said to me, "Are you grieved, Hermas? The place on the right belongs to others, who have already pleased God and suffered for the sake of the name. You still lack much in order to sit with them. But as you remain in your simplicity, remain, and you will sit with them, and so will whoever does their works and bears what they also bore." I asked, "What did they bear?" She said, "Listen: floggings, imprisonments, great tribulations, crosses, wild beasts for the sake of the name. For this reason the right side of the sanctuary belongs to them, and to whoever suffers for the name; but the left side belongs to the rest."
